blocks.text: 证明并验证 Courtade–Kumar 猜想

inlines.text: 证明并验证 Courtade–Kumar 猜想

blocks.text: 来自 Google、CUHK、USC 和 CMU 的研究人员使用 /teamwork 的长证明模式（在 Antigravity 中实现 Stellar Colosseum），在完全一般的情形下证明了信息论中的2013 年 Courtade–Kumar 猜想。该结果确认：当随机比特串通过有噪信道时，把输入压缩成单个比特的任何做法，所保留的信息都不如“独裁函数”——它只是复制单个输入比特。Gemini 首先找到了 CUHK 团队早先论文中一个推广猜想的反例。随后 CUHK 团队提出了一个新的候选函数，把该猜想归结为一个 14 变量优化问题，并给出了一个关键的分析下界。接着，Gemini 4 Argon 和更早的 Gemini 模型划分了参数空间，推导出大部分新的分析界和区间算术证书。它们还在没有人工输入的情况下，把证明从平衡函数推广到了非平衡函数。团队在 Lean 4 中形式化了整个证明，生成了 5000 万行代码。

blocks.text: 多项成果打破了处理与压缩大型矩阵和图结构长期存在的壁垒。在 STOC 2024 之前的五十年里，针对布尔矩阵乘法与三角形检测的组合算法（避开快速矩阵乘法中的代数消去）相比立方时间只节省了对数因子。一项新的确定性算法解决了 STOC 2024 的主要未解问题，实现了其相对于立方时间的目标加速。在高维几何中，一项新的下界解决了一个关于稀疏网络的未解问题，证明在任意常数因子内近似 n 个点之间的所有两两距离，可能需要多项式级多于 n 条边，即使允许额外的 Steiner 点和任意多跳。在随机线性代数中，堆叠稀疏草图解决了一个 2025 年未解问题，打破了将矩阵压缩到线性维度而不使 r 维子空间任何方向坍缩的经典稀疏性壁垒，每行只需 √log r 个非零元（比保持所有长度所需的 log r 平方级更少），并几乎匹配一个新的下界。对于动态边权插入与删除下的加权图，Stellar Colosseum 解决了 FOCS 2022 留下的一个未解问题，开发出首个割稀疏化的单遍流式算法，同时实现近最优的内存、更新时间和重建时间。

blocks.text: Proving and verifying the Courtade–Kumar conjecture

inlines.text: Proving and verifying the Courtade–Kumar conjecture

blocks.text: Researchers from Google, CUHK, USC, and CMU used /teamwork's Long Proof pattern (implementing Stellar Colosseum in Antigravity) to prove information theory's 2013 Courtade–Kumar conjecture in full generality. The result confirms that when a random bit string passes through a noisy channel, no compression of the input to a single bit preserves more information than a "dictator function", which just copies a single input bit. Gemini first found counterexamples to a generalized conjecture from the CUHK team's earlier paper. The CUHK team then proposed a new candidate function that reduced the conjecture to a 14-variable optimization problem, along with a key analytical lower bound. Gemini 4 Argon and earlier Gemini models then partitioned the parameter space and developed most of the new analytical bounds and interval-arithmetic certificates. They also extended the proof from balanced to unbalanced functions without human input. The team formalized the entire proof in Lean 4, producing 50 million lines of code.

blocks.text: Researchers also posed open problems directly to Gemini 4 and to multi-agent harnesses such as Stellar Colosseum and /teamwork, receiving end-to-end algorithms and proofs (often with Lean 4 formalizations) that the authors verified, simplified, and edited for publication. blocks.text: Several results break long standing barriers in processing and compressing large matrices and graphs. For fifty years until STOC 2024, combinatorial algorithms for Boolean matrix multiplication and triangle detection (avoiding the algebraic cancellations of fast matrix multiplication) saved only logarithmic factors over cubic time. A new deterministic algorithm resolves STOC 2024's main open question, achieving its target speedup over cubic time. In high-dimensional geometry, a new lower bound resolves an open problem on sparse networks, proving that approximating all pairwise distances among n points within any constant factor can require polynomially more than n edges, even with extra Steiner points and arbitrarily many hops. In randomized linear algebra, stacked sparse sketches resolve a 2025 open question by breaking the classical sparsity barrier for compressing a matrix to linear dimension without collapsing any direction of an r-dimensional subspace, needing only √log r nonzeros per row (quadratically fewer than the log r required to preserve all lengths) and nearly matching a new lower bound. For weighted graphs under dynamic edge-weight insertions and deletions, Stellar Colosseum resolved an open question left by FOCS 2022, developing the first single-pass streaming algorithm for cut sparsification that achieves near-optimal memory, update time, and reconstruction time simultaneously.

blocks.text: Our results also span optimization, arithmetic, data structures, and statistics. In optimization, resolving an open question on online inverse linear optimization (inferring an expert's hidden objective from decisions over time), the approach gave a deterministic algorithm achieving optimal regret while cutting runtime from exponential in the dimension to polynomial time. For n-bit integer multiplication, multi-agent campaigns simplified the theoretical Turing-machine bound below n log n, while a separate effort gave a new O(n log n) algorithm on a single two-dimensional grid whose C implementation matches the GNU Multiple Precision Arithmetic Library (GMP) bit-for-bit up to a billion bits. In data structures, another result made significant progress on Tarjan's 1985 Deque Conjecture (whether self-adjusting splay trees handle insertions and deletions at both ends in constant amortized time), proving a new upper bound on the per-operation overhead that simultaneously beats every finitely iterated inverse-Ackermann function, verified in Lean 4. Finally, in high-dimensional statistics, the approach proved that approximate leave-one-out cross-validation, which avoids refitting the model from scratch, remains accurate for non-smooth sparse penalties like elastic net.

blocks.text: Determining a molecule’s structure from experimental nuclear magnetic resonance data is one of chemistry’s hardest puzzles. For example, in HIV protease inhibitors, one misplaced bond separates an inactive look-alike from a drug. By organizing 30 specialized agents into a self-correcting loop with /teamwork and a physics-informed spectral simulator, we achieved 95% top-1 exact match and 100% top-3 accuracy on complex benchmark molecules, nearly doubling single-agent performance. Beyond teaching Gemini to reason over structure, this lays the groundwork for ongoing works on 3D protein and complex structures dynamics.

blocks.text: Generating a causal inference benchmark

We also applied a similar multi-round auditing workflow to build empirical benchmarks. Starting from five human-specified acceptance criteria like data anonymization, 29 agents running on Argon over 11.5 hours turned 13 public tables into a 50-task causal inference benchmark. In these tasks, models must determine whether a causal effect can be identified and estimate it against a known answer. After initial checks, separate reviewer and auditor agents caught shortcuts, flagged wording hints, and vetoed hallucinated scripts, turning each into a permanent test. Automating this heavily manual task generation supplies the hard problems needed to help Gemini answer counterfactual "what-if" questions.

blocks.text: Distributed systems

Using /teamwork and Argon, we built FarArray, a low-latency kernel-bypass Partitioned Global Address Space based on the SNAP microkernel. Applications built on FarArray include lock-free Connected Components, which scale to 1-trillion-edge graphs with 60x to 90x throughput gains and 40x to 180x speedups at 6x lower RAM over TCP key-value stores. Similarly, InstantEmbedding (Personalized PageRank) reduced peak DRAM by up to 14x and runtime by 11x to 27x over accelerated MapReduce implementations. The team also used /teamwork and Argon to create custom TPU kernels for Graph Neural Networks, delivering up to a 185x High Bandwidth Memory reduction and 8x to 15x speedups in forward and backward passes. Further details are available in our recent Antigravity blog post.

blocks.text: Autonomous hill climbing

To test autonomous optimization over long horizons, hill-climbing teams on Argon trained a 9x9 Go engine from scratch starting from a basic AlphaZero implementation. Human researchers set the chip allocation and evaluation setup, while the harness ran autonomous campaigns for faster self-play (achieving a 2,300x speedup) and faster Elo readings, promoting champions strictly via statistical tests on locked records. In under eight days, the engine gained roughly 2,600 Elo, reaching 1,885 Elo, placing it between KataGo at 16 and 32 visits per move.

inlines.text: Memory-safe Rust rewrites, /boost, and TPU kernel optimization

blocks.text: Large code migrations fail when agents stub out dependencies or alter tests to make a broken port pass. A new /teamwork rewrite pattern, soon to be available in Antigravity, solved this by scheduling each module only after its dependencies compile, linking every leaf module against the original, unmodified test suite. Building on the initial 25% port of the Zircon microkernel, a two-week Argon campaign rewrote the remaining C++ code, adding about 800,000 lines of safe Rust that pass all kernel unit tests and boot on arm64 hardware. /teamwork also rewrote libgav1, Google's AV1 video decoder, from C++ into around 170k lines Rust, achieving 100% bit-exact parity across a broad conformance test suite. Initially, the port was around 4x slower than the original C++ code. However, after giving /teamwork access to profiling tools and a mandate to maximize speed on sample video clips, the Rust port became 20-30% faster than the original C++ and hand-optimized assembly code on both x86_64 and ARM.

Using /teamwork's DuoDiscover pattern on Argon, four parallel agents identified performance bottlenecks and constructed fast, 23-second proxy evaluators called yardsticks. Upcoming updates will bring our formal proof pattern and additional specialized workflows into Antigravity.
